title: Ketel Marte’s green hat had a ‘burning bridges’ message. He says it meant nothing.
content:
PHOENIX — Ketel Marte on Tuesday told The Athletic a neon green hat he wore one night earlier, which displayed the message “May the bridges I burn light the way” and quickly went viral on social media, carried no extra meaning for the embattled Arizona Diamondbacks star, who was returning to the team after a long absence.

“I didn’t know what it was,” Marte told The Athletic when asked why he chose that hat specifically.

The neon green trucker-style hat served as a curious choice after Marte spent 13 games away from the team following a no-show at Fenway Park, three of those games on MLB’s restricted list without pay.

Marte, a native of the Dominican Republic whose first language is Spanish, uses a team interpreter in interviews. He was read a direct translation of the message.

“I didn’t know I had that hat on,” Marte said, adding, “I didn’t know, I just put it on.”

Asked directly whether the message meant anything in particular, Marte said no, affirming it was just a hat.

His manager, Torey Lovullo, was asked a similar question and instead offered a different outlook on Marte’s fashion choices.

“I want to move past this Ketel stuff as quickly as possible,” Lovullo said. “I think if you chop up those words, maybe he’s taking some accountability. He feels like he’s done some things, and he wants to get better. That’s how I read it.”

Whether intentional or not, the hat was another element of a saga that stretches four seasons in which Marte has gone AWOL from the Diamondbacks.

After 10 days on the injured list with left knee inflammation, Marte made his return to Chase Field on Monday, addressing the media before holding court in the Diamondbacks’ home clubhouse, where he apologized to his teammates. The Diamondbacks lost 2-1, and Marte went 1-for-3 with a single and a walk.

“He’s here,” third baseman Nolan Arenado said of Marte’s meeting. “He’s ready to help us win ballgames, and that’s it. To be quite honest, I’m kind of tired of talking about it. So I’m just not gonna talk about it anymore. He’s here. We want the best for him. We want the best for this group, and he makes our group better. So we just want to go out there and compete.”

Tuesday, Marte was once again slotted fourth in the lineup at DH. He’s expected to resume duties at second base as early as Wednesday’s series finale against the Philadelphia Phillies or Arizona’s road opener against the Houston Astros on Friday.
